findings.description: The submodule-planting fixture (move `sub/.git` to `.git/modules/sub`, arm `diff.external`/textconv/fsmonitor, write `info/attributes`, loop over the shared-config keys) is written out in land.test.ts, merge-gate-regate.test.ts and git-diff-client.test.ts, and the copies already plant different keys. This is the third use, so a shared helper in `test/helpers/` would keep a new production pin from being planted in only some suites.

The *Rejected* paragraph credits `GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=none` to decision 73, but 0073 never mentions it. That pin is recorded in 0089 (and 0059), so a maintainer following the 0073 reference won't find it. Cite 0089 instead.

land-remeasure's `changed()` runs `git diff --name-only` without the `--ignore-submodules=none` this PR adds to DIFF_SAFE_FLAGS. Its output is the only input to the `critical` check that makes `pup land --remeasure` wait for `--approved-by`. So a gitlink a session bumps past the pin under a CRITICAL_PATHS area (e.g. `.github/actions/setup`), with `diff.ignoreSubmodules=all` set in the shared config, is dropped from the listing and lands with no approval. The `linked` ls-tree check only covers ADAPTER_PATHS. `fix-round.service.ts:570-580` (`differing`) has the same gap, with lower impact.

The conductor's security-review diff (`securityReviewGit`) builds its own pins and never got `diff.submodule=short`. It patches with `--ignore-submodules=none`, so under a `diff.submodule=diff` config a gitlink in the range starts a child git in the submodule, and that submodule's `diff.external` or textconv runs as the operator. That breaks ADR 0203's claim that no diff starts a git in a submodule's repo. Adding `--submodule=short` to `diffArgs` closes it.

process_issues.description: Skipped review-context (no CORS/HTTP/docker/CI/settings surface; git protocol semantics covered by correctness and security), review-spec (no closing issue or spec source), review-workflow-safety (no .github/workflows change) and review-maintainability (off the default roster). Dropped the guards reviewer's nit about adding `Amended by:` back-references to 0073/0101: docs/adr/README.md says not to add `Amended by:` lines to a landed decision.
The reviewer tried `bash scripts/adr-index.sh`, which the CI lock refused; it found the ADRs with Grep instead.
